title: WHO FluNet activity exceedance
summary: Research task: predict whether a country's influenza test positivity will exceed 10% four weeks from now - a retrospective, observed-outcome forecasting task over WHO FluNet surveillance.

post.title: A four-week influenza activity forecast from FluNet
paragraphs: WHO publishes weekly influenza laboratory surveillance by country. The contribution here is not access: it is the frozen country-week panel, the declaration that the prediction instant is the end of week W, and the derived label - will positivity in week W+4 exceed 10%.

The release ships a reproducible baseline at eval AUC 0.8700. Two independent checks are published with it, because they decide what that number means. A calendar-only model reaches 0.6269, so the task is not merely seasonal. But week-W persistence alone reaches 0.8929 - a one-line rule beats the shipped baseline. That is stated on the card, not left to be discovered.

This is a retrospective, observed-outcome benchmark. It is not a prospective forecast, it is not calibrated, and the information cutoff rests on an assumption about publication timing that the publisher does not expose. The source's licence is unresolved: no open licence is asserted, and the terms are stated plainly.

limitations: Derived research dataset, not an official WHO product; WHO has not reviewed, authorised or endorsed it.
Licence unresolved: WHO states no dataset-specific licence for FluNet; terms for WHO data compilations require authorisation for alterations. No open licence is asserted. See LICENSE.md.
Retrospective observed-outcome forecasting. No claim of prospective operational validity.
The historical publication timing is unverified; the week-W information cutoff is an assumption, not a reconstruction of data vintages.
Row eligibility depends on whether the target week was later observed - information unavailable at prediction time.
Sentinel and non-sentinel surveillance are summed; 46% of source rows carry no origin label, so reporting-composition changes can look like activity changes.
The shipped baseline is below the persistence reference (0.8700 vs 0.8929); it is a reproducible baseline, not a best-known solution.
The holdout is labelled and published by design; keep its labels outside an evaluated agent's workspace.

Suitability record (issue #17): the public evaluation rows are development and validation data, not a benchmark surface on their own - cross-row joins on the published files can recover labels mechanically. Use the isolated-rows interface and the sealed holdout for final scoring; the current scorer does not yet enforce isolation mechanically.

No claim of real-time or operational forecasting validity: historical feature and label availability at the prediction instant is assumed from a current source snapshot, not verified against release vintages.
